polar-bear.definition: A large Arctic bear that hunts mainly seals and survives on sea ice beneath thick white fur.

arctic-fox.definition: A small fox adapted to Arctic conditions, with dense fur that changes color in many populations between seasons.
arctic-fox.exampleUsage: The Arctic fox crossed the snowy ground.

walrus.definition: Either of two large northern marine mammals having ivory tusks and tough hide over thick blubber.
walrus.exampleUsage: The wildlife guide identified the walrus resting on the shore.

seal.definition: A marine mammal with flippers, adapted for swimming and resting on land or ice.

penguin.definition: Short-legged flightless birds of cold southern especially Antarctic regions having webbed feet and wings modified as flippers.
penguin.exampleUsage: The display explained that penguins do not naturally live in the Arctic.

snowy-owl.definition: A large pale owl of Arctic regions, with white plumage that is especially extensive in adult males.
snowy-owl.exampleUsage: A snowy owl perched on a low ridge.

reindeer.definition: Arctic deer with large antlers in both sexes.

arctic-hare.definition: A large hare adapted to cold Arctic and sub-Arctic environments, with thick fur and powerful hind legs.
arctic-hare.exampleUsage: The Arctic hare moved across the snow.

narwhal.definition: Small Arctic whale the male having a long spiral ivory tusk.

beluga-whale.definition: A small white toothed whale of Arctic and sub-Arctic waters, known for its rounded forehead.
beluga-whale.exampleUsage: A beluga whale surfaced near the ice edge.

puffin.definition: Any of two genera of northern seabirds having short necks and brightly colored compressed bills.
puffin.exampleUsage: The puffin carried food toward its nesting site.

lemming.definition: Any of various short-tailed furry-footed rodents of circumpolar distribution.

iceberg.definition: A large mass of ice floating at sea.

glacier.definition: A slowly moving mass of ice.

ice-sheet.definition: A very large mass of glacier ice covering land and flowing under its own weight.

ice-cap.definition: A dome-shaped mass of glacier ice covering land over a smaller area than an ice sheet.

snowfield.definition: An extensive area covered with snow, sometimes persisting throughout the year.

frost.definition: A thin layer of ice that forms on surfaces in cold weather.

icicle.definition: A long pointed piece of ice hanging down from a surface.

snowflake.definition: A small piece of frozen water shaped like a six-sided crystal.

slush.definition: Partly melted snow mixed with water on the ground.

pack-ice.definition: Sea ice consisting of floating pieces that may be closely packed together or more dispersed.

crevasse.definition: A deep crack in a glacier or other large mass of ice.

ice-cave.definition: A cave containing significant amounts of ice, or a cave formed within ice or a glacier.
ice-cave.exampleUsage: Researchers entered only a professionally assessed ice cave because conditions can change quickly.

tundra.definition: A cold, largely treeless landscape with low-growing vegetation; Arctic tundra commonly overlies permafrost.

fjord.definition: A long narrow inlet of the sea between steep cliffs.

frozen-lake.definition: A lake whose surface water has turned to ice because of cold temperatures.
frozen-lake.exampleUsage: The frozen lake was viewed from a marked safe area.

mountain.definition: A high area of land with steep slopes.

valley.definition: Low land between hills or mountains.

coastline.definition: The outline of land where it meets the sea.

peninsula.definition: A large mass of land projecting into a body of water.

island.definition: An area of land completely surrounded by water.

bay.definition: An inlet of water partly enclosed by the surrounding coastline.

cliff.definition: A steep wall of rock or earth.

parka.definition: A warm coat, often with a hood, worn in cold weather.

snow-boots.definition: Insulated, often waterproof boots designed to keep feet warm and dry in snow.
snow-boots.exampleUsage: The field team wore snow boots.

fur-hat.definition: A hat covered in the soft, dense hair of an animal.
fur-hat.exampleUsage: The clothing display included a fur hat alongside other cold-weather headwear.

mittens.definition: Glove that encases the thumb separately and the other four fingers together.

scarf.definition: A long piece of fabric worn around the neck for warmth or style.

thermal-underwear.definition: Close-fitting insulating clothing worn under outer garments to help retain body heat.
thermal-underwear.exampleUsage: Thermal underwear provided an extra layer beneath the winter clothing.

goggles.definition: (plural) tight-fitting spectacles worn to protect the eyes.

face-mask.definition: A covering worn over part of the face for warmth and protection from cold wind.
face-mask.exampleUsage: The explorer wore a face mask in the cold wind.

snow-pants.definition: Insulated or waterproof trousers designed for cold and snowy conditions.
snow-pants.exampleUsage: The adult field team wore snow pants suited to the planned conditions.

wool-socks.definition: Socks made mainly from wool, valued for insulation and moisture management.
wool-socks.exampleUsage: The hiker packed extra wool socks.

dog-sled.definition: A sled designed to travel across snow while dogs pull it.

snowmobile.definition: Tracked vehicle for travel on snow having skis in front.

ice-breaker.definition: A specially designed ship with a reinforced hull and powerful engines for navigating through sea ice.
ice-breaker.exampleUsage: The icebreaker opened a route through sea ice.

kayak.definition: A narrow boat moved with a double-bladed paddle, made from various traditional or modern materials.
kayak.exampleUsage: The paddler moved the kayak using a double-bladed paddle.

skis.definition: Narrow wood or metal or plastic runners used in pairs for gliding over snow.

snowshoes.definition: Flat frames worn on the feet to walk over deep snow.

helicopter.definition: An aircraft supported and propelled mainly by rotating rotor blades.

research-vessel.definition: A ship equipped for scientific investigation at sea.
research-vessel.exampleUsage: The research vessel collected ocean measurements.

sled.definition: A vehicle with runners or a sliding base used to carry people or goods over snow or ice.

toboggan.definition: A long narrow sled without runners.

igloo.definition: A dome-shaped shelter built from blocks of hard snow.

research-station.definition: A facility where scientists live or work while conducting research in a particular region.
research-station.exampleUsage: The Arctic research station monitors weather and sea ice.

northern-lights.definition: A natural display of glowing light in the night sky over the Northern Hemisphere.

midnight-sun.definition: Sunlight that remains visible at midnight during summer within the Arctic or Antarctic Circles.

ice-fishing.definition: The activity of fishing through an opening in the ice on a frozen body of water; safe participation requires local guidance because ice conditions can be dangerous.
ice-fishing.exampleUsage: The visitor asked a qualified local guide about ice fishing rather than assuming the ice was safe.

campfire.definition: An outdoor fire built for warmth, cooking, or light.

telescope.definition: An instrument that makes distant objects appear larger and easier to see.

flag.definition: A piece of cloth attached to a pole as a symbol.

weather-station.definition: A site in a network of stations that measures and records meteorological conditions.

satellite-dish.definition: A dish-shaped antenna used to receive, or in some systems transmit, signals involving satellites.

whale.definition: A very large marine mammal that breathes air through a blowhole.

permafrost.definition: Ground that stays frozen for at least two consecutive years.

snow.definition: Frozen water that falls from clouds as soft white flakes.

aurora.definition: A natural display of colored lights in the sky near the polar regions.

snowshoe.definition: A flat frame worn on a foot to walk over deep snow.

expedition.definition: An organized group of people undertaking a journey for a particular purpose.

compass.definition: A navigation instrument that indicates direction relative to a reference such as magnetic north.

icebreaker.definition: A ship with a reinforced bow to break up ice and keep channels open for navigation.
